bug_semantics: The authenticated GET /get_history_details endpoint loads a retained history row by caller-controlled history_id, then loads its parent conversion. The repository lookup deliberately returns None for a soft-deleted conversion. The vulnerable guard authorized only when the parent existed (`if conversion_obj and ...`), so a missing/deleted parent skipped the denial and the endpoint returned conversion_history.to_json(), including retained input_text, old_output_text, and new_output_text, to any logged-in user who could request that history ID.
flaw_origin: Commit 37d7ba64638ad78f4604725f81bafac497ca235a introduced the exact fail-open mechanism in one ordinary commit: it added @login_required and a parent-visibility check to get_history_details, but made that check conditional on a truthy parent, while simultaneously changing get_convert() to exclude inactive soft-deleted conversions by default and return None. Thus deletion made the authorization subject disappear and the new conditional treated that state as authorized. Later renames/repository extraction and 9a8a78d1df3ca96f8d26884b8a08e03a7260c925's access.can_see refactor preserved the outer `conversion_obj and` condition rather than originating the flaw.
ai_marker: absent: `git cat-file -p 37d7ba64638ad78f4604725f81bafac497ca235a` shows human author and committer ecrou-exact <geffetheo@gmail.com> and only the subject `fix: [secruity] correction of potential security problem`; there is no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI trailer, or bot identity in the BIC commit object.
evidence: The assigned GitHub advisory GHSA-9P5Q-96WV-4XVH / CVE-2026-72759 identifies https://github.com/MISP/cti-transmute/commit/88dc65f0117cf7a120f6252674c529e7b9c9b8c3 and describes disclosure of retained history data after its conversion is deleted. `git show 88dc65f0117cf7a120f6252674c529e7b9c9b8c3` shows the direct one-line authorization correction in website/web/conversions/conversions.py: `if conversion_obj and not access.can_see(...)` becomes `if not conversion_obj or not access.can_see(...)`, with comments explicitly stating that deleted conversions resolve to None and history input/output otherwise leaks. `git diff 37d7ba64638ad78f4604725f81bafac497ca235a^ 37d7ba64638ad78f4604725f81bafac497ca235a -- website/web/convert/convert.py website/web/convert/convert_core.py` shows the BIC adding @login_required, loading the parent, and guarding only under `if convert_obj and not convert_obj.public`, while changing get_convert(convert_id) from an unconditional `Convert.query.get(convert_id)` to a default-excluding lookup that returns None when `not convert.is_active`. Direct parent-tree reads (`git show 18b09206dd680c405ad47480c964a1adb76d8020:<path>`) confirm that parent has neither the new parent-authorization conditional nor the deleted-record-to-None lookup; those exact coupled semantics are absent. The parent did expose the endpoint without authorization, but 37d7ba6 is the smallest commit that created the advisory's specific residual deleted-parent fail-open after attempting to harden the endpoint. `git log -L` traces the conditional through renames and the 9a8a78d1df3ca96f8d26884b8a08e03a7260c925 shared-predicate refactor to the fix; the latter retained the truthiness gate. Tag containment gives the repository version boundary: the BIC is absent from v1.2 and contained by v1.3, v1.4, and v1.5; the fix is absent from v1.4 and contained only by v1.5. GitHub publishes no formal affected-version range for this advisory, so these are repository-history boundaries rather than an asserted package range. `git merge-base` returns the BIC itself for BIC/fix, proving the direct fix is on its descendant line. `git cat-file -p` gives parent 18b09206dd680c405ad47480c964a1adb76d8020 and the marker-free human commit object.
reasoning: The security property is fail-closed authorization of retained history when its parent conversion cannot be resolved. The original endpoint predated the BIC and was broadly unauthenticated; that is not the narrower mechanism corrected by the advisory fix. The May 18 hardening commit is the causal minimum for the described bug because it introduced both facts required for the residual bypass: deleted parents now resolve to None, and authorization runs only for non-None parents. Its immediate parent lacks both coupled changes. Subsequent moves and predicate centralization preserved the flaw, so they are not BICs; the July 22 commit is the direct fix because it changes the same guard to deny either a missing parent or failed visibility. The candidate is a normal single-parent commit, not a squash aggregate. Since the BIC commit object contains no AI authorship/co-authorship/generation marker and identifies only a human author/committer, the BIC-only attribution rule yields NOT_AI.
